state:
**Goal `tooling-overhaul`: every stage is on disk, Stage 12 included.** The cutover is on `main`. `main` stays frozen until the driver reaches the goal, and tag `pre-overhaul` is the rollback.

The red `npm` checks after session 0006 were the driver judging with stale code, not a regression: that turn imported `tools/nv/lib/proc.ts` before session 0006 committed the `Bun.which` fix, and `bun nv loop --run --name "vsix packages"` and `--name "vscode (headless)"` are green on the tree. A turn now takes a `driverFiles` snapshot before its session, and a session that changes imported driver code is judged by a fresh turn with no session of its own (`tools/nv/driver/launch.ts`'s `driverChanged`, `tools/nv/cmd/loop.ts`'s `serve`), which is what the Python driver did.

ADR 0221 (`docs/decisions/0221.md`) records the data model, the Bun runtime and the generated-output rule. The goal-end gates are green: `bun nv owners --closes tooling-overhaul` and `bun nv playbook --closes tooling-overhaul` name nothing. The Python launch shims are deleted, and a run starts with `bun nv loop`, which switches to the next goal itself when this one is reached.

`bun nv decisions --check` reports 44 records without a plain-language summary, 0221 among them. It is not a gate; `bun nv decisions --gate` passes.
